# 1 Clement Chapter 33 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 33

**33:1** So what are we to do, brothers? Shall we sit back, stop doing good, and abandon love? God forbid that this should happen to us! Rather, let us press on with earnestness and zeal to accomplish every good work.

**33:2** Consider: the Creator and Master of all things himself takes delight in his own works.

**33:3** By his almighty power he established the heavens. By his unsearchable wisdom he set them in order. He separated the earth from the surrounding waters and set it firm on the unshakable foundation of his own will. By his command he brought into being the living creatures that walk upon it. And having prepared the sea and all its creatures beforehand, he enclosed them by his power.

**33:4** And then, best of all — the greatest and most excellent work of his mind — he formed humanity with his own holy and faultless hands in the likeness of his image.

**33:5** For God said: "Let us make humanity in our image and our likeness." And God made humanity; male and female he made them.

**33:6** When he had finished all this, he praised it and blessed it and said: "Be fruitful and multiply."

**33:7** Notice that all the righteous were adorned with good works. Even the Lord himself adorned himself with his works and rejoiced in them.

**33:8** So since we have this pattern, let us without delay apply ourselves to his will, and with every ounce of our strength let us do the works of righteousness.

---

*PNEUMA renders the creation section with vivid, paragraph-style flow while maintaining the argument that God's own delight in good work is the model for human behavior.*
